key_insight: Combining crystal-structure GNN outputs with an LLM text branch improves overall accuracy for predicting four magnetic-ordering classes over either standalone model.
engineering_relevance: The approach could support computational screening of magnetic materials before costly laboratory characterization.
method: Encode crystal structures with a graph neural network.
Process semantic descriptions of material properties and structure with an LLM.
Fuse outputs using three strategies to classify non-magnetic, ferromagnetic, antiferromagnetic, or ferrimagnetic ordering.
evidence_signal: Evaluation uses combined Materials Project, Magndata, and experimentally characterized uranium-compound data with an 80/10/10 training/validation/test split; the abstract reports improved overall accuracy but no numerical scores.
watch_item: Text descriptions should be checked for magnetic-label leakage to ensure gains reflect predictive information rather than disclosed answers.
paper_title: Crystal Structure Based Graph Neural Network And LLM Multi-Modal Approach for Material Magnetic Ordering Prediction
